claims.evidence: MedlinePlus: dutasteride used for benign prostatic hyperplasia (enlarged prostate); belongs to 5-alpha reductase inhibitors.
claims.newSentence: MedlinePlus (a US source) says dutasteride is used to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia, an enlarged prostate gland, and belongs to the 5-alpha reductase inhibitors.

claims.evidence: NHS About finasteride: for hair loss only on private prescription, not on the NHS; still licensed on NHS for enlarged prostate.

StatPearls dutasteride page describes inhibition of types I and II only; the 'all 3 isoenzymes / 99%' wording appears on the finasteride StatPearls page and conflicts with other reviews. Dutasteride lowering serum DHT more than finasteride is supported by PMC1550785 (dual inhibitor, near-complete suppression) and PMC2809314 (head-to-head: about 94.7% vs 70.8%); PMC10080355 says finasteride is type 2 selective.
claims.newSentence: Reviews describe dutasteride as blocking both type 1 and type 2 of the 5-alpha reductase enzyme, whereas finasteride mainly blocks type 2, and dutasteride lowers blood DHT further than finasteride does.

claims.evidence: PMC5407420 systematic review: insufficient evidence that either finasteride or dutasteride offers an advantage in efficacy or safety for clinically important outcomes.

Retrieved MedlinePlus text did not show the side-effect list (erection, sex drive, ejaculation, breast changes). StatPearls dutasteride gives impotence, decreased libido, difficulty ejaculating and advises reporting breast enlargement or tenderness.
claims.newSentence: StatPearls lists erection problems, reduced sex drive and difficulty ejaculating among the sexual side effects of dutasteride, and advises that breast enlargement or tenderness be reported.

claims.evidence: StatPearls dutasteride: sexual adverse effects may persist despite discontinuation (another StatPearls page calls this rare).
NHS Who can and cannot take finasteride: most men 18 or over can take it; generally not recommended for women or children.
NHS page lists depression or thoughts of harming themselves, severe bladder problems and liver problems among things to tell a doctor.
NHS Fertility and pregnancy page: harm to a pregnant partner or baby from a man taking finasteride is very unlikely.

MedlinePlus excerpt confirms women who are or may become pregnant should not handle capsules, but blood-donation advice was not found on MedlinePlus (only in a trial consent form, six months after stopping). Blood-donation clause removed.
claims.newSentence: MedlinePlus (a US source) says dutasteride is for use only in men, and that women who are or may become pregnant should not handle dutasteride capsules.

claims.evidence: NHS side-effects page: call 999 or go to A&E if thoughts of harming yourself; About page: mood changes such as depression/self-harm thoughts, speak to doctor. NHS 111 and Samaritans not in retrieved NHS finasteride text; they are the site's generic routes. Original wording (call 111 for self-harm thoughts) did not match NHS wording, so reworded.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says anyone with thoughts of harming themselves should call 999 or go to A&E; for low mood or distress, NHS 111 (mental health option) and Samaritans on 116 123, free at any time, can help.

notes: c01 supported but edited only to mark MedlinePlus as US source (c01/c05/c10 all carry the US marker). c03: first-pass claim of 'all three forms' not on the dutasteride StatPearls page; replaced with type 1+2 wording, comparison cited to PMC1550785/PMC2809314 (PMC10080355 for finasteride type 2). Add those URLs to the ledger for c03; c05 now cites StatPearls only. c11: NHS 111 and Samaritans were not found on the NHS finasteride pages; retained as the site signposting rule (textbook), and NHS finasteride pages direct self-harm thoughts to 999/A&E. No doses or 'safe' wording remain. MHRA May 2026 Drug Safety Update on finasteride/dutasteride psychiatric and sexual effects exists on gov.uk but was not used.
